title: Luke Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Luke chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Luke Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Luke Chapter 7.

questions.question: In Luke 7, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: A centurion sent elders to Jesus
Jesus raised a dead man in Nain
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus entered into Capernaum
questions.explanation: Jesus entering Capernaum is mentioned in Luke 7:1, which is the earliest event in the chapter.

questions.question: Who was the centurion concerned about in Luke 7?
questions.correctAnswer: His servant
questions.explanation: The centurion's servant was sick and dear to him, mentioned in Luke 7:2.

questions.question: How did the centurion communicate his request to Jesus?
options: He sent the elders of the Jews to Jesus
He sent a messenger with a gift
questions.correctAnswer: He sent the elders of the Jews to Jesus
questions.explanation: The centurion sent the elders of the Jews to Jesus to ask for his servant's healing, as stated in Luke 7:3.

questions.question: Why did the elders say the centurion was worthy for Jesus to help him?
options: Because he loved their nation and built them a synagogue
Because he was a Roman official
Because he was a good friend of Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: Because he loved their nation and built them a synagogue
questions.explanation: The elders said the centurion loved their nation and had built them a synagogue, Luke 7:5.

questions.question: What did the centurion say to Jesus about entering his house?
options: Lord, trouble not thyself: for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter under my roof
I invite you to a feast
My house is ready for you
questions.correctAnswer: Lord, trouble not thyself: for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter under my roof
questions.explanation: The centurion sent friends to tell Jesus not to trouble himself to come under his roof because he felt unworthy, Luke 7:6.

questions.question: What did the centurion say about his own authority?
options: I say unto one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh
I command the soldiers to fight
questions.correctAnswer: I say unto one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh
questions.explanation: The centurion described his authority over soldiers and that his orders are obeyed immediately, Luke 7:8.

questions.question: How did Jesus respond to the centurion's expression of faith?
options: He marvelled and said he had not found so great faith in Israel
questions.correctAnswer: He marvelled and said he had not found so great faith in Israel
questions.explanation: Jesus marveled at the centurion's faith and told the people he had not found so great faith in Israel, Luke 7:9.

questions.question: What was the condition of the centurion's servant when those sent by Jesus returned?
questions.correctAnswer: The servant was whole
questions.explanation: The servants sent by Jesus found the centurion's servant healed and whole, Luke 7:10.

questions.question: Where did Jesus go the day after healing the centurion's servant?
questions.correctAnswer: A city called Nain
questions.explanation: Jesus went into a city called Nain the day after, Luke 7:11.

questions.question: What was the relationship of the dead man being carried out of Nain?
options: He was the only son of his mother, and she was a widow
He was the mayor of the city
questions.correctAnswer: He was the only son of his mother, and she was a widow
questions.explanation: The dead man was the only son of his mother, who was a widow, Luke 7:12.

questions.question: What did Jesus say to the widow in Nain?
questions.correctAnswer: Weep not
questions.explanation: Jesus told the widow, "Weep not," as recorded in Luke 7:13.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus had compassion on the widow when he saw her.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 7:13 states that the Lord had compassion on the widow when he saw her.

questions.question: True or False: The people glorified God and said a great prophet had risen among them after Jesus raised the dead man.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: After Jesus raised the dead man, the people glorified God and said a great prophet had risen among them, Luke 7:16.

questions.question: True or False: The text says Jesus performed a miracle by turning water into wine.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not mention Jesus turning water into wine; this miracle is not in Luke 7.

questions.question: True or False: The chapter records that Jesus was angry with the centurion for not inviting him to his house.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text records no anger from Jesus about the centurion not inviting him; instead, Jesus marveled at his faith, Luke 7:6-9.

medium.title: Luke Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Luke Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did John the Baptist send his disciples to ask Jesus?
options: Are you the one who is to come?
Are you the son of God?
questions.correctAnswer: Are you the one who is to come?
questions.explanation: This is found in Luke 7:19, where John sent his disciples to ask Jesus if He is the one who should come or if they should look for another.

questions.question: What does Luke 7:22 promise will happen if someone believes in Jesus' works?
options: The blind will see and the lame will walk.
questions.correctAnswer: The blind will see and the lame will walk.
questions.explanation: Luke 7:22 details the miracles Jesus performed, which serve as evidence of His identity.

questions.question: What did Jesus tell the messengers to report back to John?
options: What they have seen and heard.
That John is greater than Him.
questions.correctAnswer: What they have seen and heard.
questions.explanation: In Luke 7:22, Jesus instructed the messengers to tell John about the miracles they witnessed.

questions.question: In Luke 7:30, who rejected the counsel of God?
questions.correctAnswer: The Pharisees and lawyers.
questions.explanation: Luke 7:30 states that the Pharisees and lawyers rejected God’s counsel by not being baptized by John.

questions.question: According to Luke 7:23, who is blessed?
options: Those who are not offended in Jesus.
questions.correctAnswer: Those who are not offended in Jesus.
questions.explanation: Jesus declares in Luke 7:23 that blessed are those who are not offended by Him.

questions.question: What metaphor does Jesus use to describe the generation in Luke 7:32?
options: A reed shaken in the wind.
questions.correctAnswer: Children in the marketplace.
questions.explanation: In Luke 7:32, Jesus compares the generation to children sitting in the marketplace, illustrating their fickleness.

questions.question: What does Jesus say about John the Baptist in Luke 7:28?
options: He is less than the least in the kingdom of God.
He is a glutton and a drunkard.
He is a reed shaken by the wind.
questions.correctAnswer: He is the greatest prophet.
questions.explanation: Jesus states in Luke 7:28 that among those born of women, there is no greater prophet than John the Baptist.

questions.question: What did the publicans do in response to John's baptism according to Luke 7:29?
questions.correctAnswer: They justified God.
questions.explanation: Luke 7:29 notes that the people and publicans justified God by being baptized with John's baptism.

questions.question: In Luke 7:21, what did Jesus cure during the same hour?
questions.correctAnswer: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Luke 7:21 states that Jesus cured many infirmities, plagues, evil spirits, and gave sight to the blind.

questions.question: What did Jesus mean by saying that John the Baptist was more than a prophet in Luke 7:26?
questions.correctAnswer: He fulfilled prophecy.
questions.explanation: In Luke 7:26, Jesus highlights that John is more than a prophet as he fulfills the role of the messenger preparing the way for the Lord.

questions.question: What role did the centurion's servant have in Luke 7:2?
options: He was sick and ready to die.
He was a friend of Jesus.
questions.correctAnswer: He was sick and ready to die.
questions.explanation: Luke 7:2 states that the centurion's servant was dear to him but was sick and near death.

questions.question: What does Luke 7:33 say about John the Baptist's lifestyle?
options: He came neither eating bread nor drinking wine.
questions.correctAnswer: He came neither eating bread nor drinking wine.
questions.explanation: Luke 7:33 mentions that John the Baptist lived a strict lifestyle, abstaining from bread and wine.

questions.question: Does Luke 7:34 say that Jesus was accused of being a friend of sinners?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 7:34 indicates that Jesus was labeled as a friend of publicans and sinners, reflecting the criticism He faced.

questions.question: Is it true that the Pharisees accepted John's baptism according to Luke 7:30?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 7:30 states that the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God by not being baptized by John.

questions.question: Did Jesus perform any miracles in response to John's disciples in Luke 7:21?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 7:21 confirms that Jesus cured many infirmities and gave sight to the blind during that hour.

hard.title: Luke Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Luke Chapter 7.

questions.question: In Luke 7:42, what question does Jesus ask Simon regarding the two debtors?
options: Tell me therefore, which of them will love him most?
Tell me, which of them paid their debts?
questions.correctAnswer: Tell me therefore, which of them will love him most?
questions.explanation: Luke 7:42 records Jesus asking Simon, 'Tell me therefore, which of them will love him most?' highlighting the connection between forgiveness and love.

questions.question: According to Luke 7:44, what did Simon fail to provide Jesus when He entered his house?
questions.correctAnswer: Water for his feet
questions.explanation: Luke 7:44 states Jesus pointed out that Simon 'gavest me no water for my feet,' contrasting Simon’s lack of hospitality with the woman’s actions.

questions.question: In Luke 7:47, Jesus explains the relationship between forgiveness and love. What is the key statement?
options: Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little.
He who forgives shall be forgiven in turn.
Love covers a multitude of sins.
questions.correctAnswer: Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little.
questions.explanation: Luke 7:47 directly states this principle linking the extent of forgiveness to the extent of love shown.

questions.question: What is the reaction of those who sat at meat with Jesus after He said 'Thy sins are forgiven' to the woman in Luke 7:49?
options: Who is this that forgiveth sins also?
questions.correctAnswer: Who is this that forgiveth sins also?
questions.explanation: Luke 7:49 records the internal questioning of those present: 'Who is this that forgiveth sins also?' highlighting the divine authority of Jesus.

questions.question: According to Luke 7:38, what actions did the woman take at Jesus' feet?
options: She washed his feet with tears, wiped them with her hair, kissed his feet, and anointed them with ointment.
She sat beside him and listened.
She gave him bread and wine.
She anointed his head with oil.
questions.correctAnswer: She washed his feet with tears, wiped them with her hair, kissed his feet, and anointed them with ointment.
questions.explanation: Luke 7:38 vividly describes the woman's acts of devotion and repentance at Jesus' feet.

questions.question: In Luke 7:41, how much did the two debtors owe the creditor respectively?
options: One owed five hundred pence, and the other fifty.
One owed five hundred pence, and the other five.
One owed fifty pence, and the other five hundred.
questions.correctAnswer: One owed five hundred pence, and the other fifty.
questions.explanation: Luke 7:41 specifies the amounts owed were five hundred pence and fifty pence respectively.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'λογίζομαι' (logizomai) in Luke 7:43 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: To reckon or to judge
questions.explanation: In Luke 7:43, 'λογίζομαι' is used in the context of Simon judging rightly, meaning 'to reckon' or 'to judge' a matter correctly.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Luke 7:41–43 with the story of the two debtors?
questions.correctAnswer: Parable
questions.explanation: Luke 7:41–43 uses a parable, a narrative device Jesus commonly used to teach spiritual truths through simple stories.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of forgiveness and love seen in Luke 7:47?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 103:12
questions.explanation: Psalm 103:12 speaks of God's forgiveness and removal of sins, connecting with Luke 7:47’s theme of forgiveness leading to love.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects to the theme of faith saving the woman in Luke 7:50?
questions.correctAnswer: Mark 5:34
questions.explanation: Mark 5:34 parallels Luke 7:50 where Jesus declares to the woman, 'Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole,' emphasizing faith’s role in salvation.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the story of the woman anointing Jesus’ feet in Luke 7:36?
options: Jesus declares, 'But wisdom is justified of all her children' in verse 35.
Jesus raises the widow’s son at Nain.
John the Baptist sends messengers to Jesus.
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus declares, 'But wisdom is justified of all her children' in verse 35.
questions.explanation: Luke 7:35 directly precedes verse 36, serving as a thematic introduction to the Pharisee’s invitation and the woman’s anointing.

questions.question: What is the typological significance of the woman anointing Jesus' feet with ointment in Luke 7:38?
options: It foreshadows Jesus' burial anointing as in John 12:3.
It represents a Roman purification ritual.
It signifies the anointing of kings in the Old Testament.
It symbolizes the washing of hands before meals.
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Jesus' burial anointing as in John 12:3.
questions.explanation: The woman's anointing in Luke 7:38 prefigures the burial anointing of Jesus described in John 12:3, showing a typological connection.

questions.question: How does Luke 7:39 illustrate the Pharisee’s skepticism towards Jesus?
options: The Pharisee doubts Jesus is a prophet because he allows a sinner woman to touch him.
The Pharisee accuses Jesus of eating too much.
The Pharisee offers Jesus a seat of honor.
questions.correctAnswer: The Pharisee doubts Jesus is a prophet because he allows a sinner woman to touch him.
questions.explanation: Luke 7:39 shows the Pharisee's internal judgment that if Jesus were truly a prophet, he would know the woman’s sinful status and not permit her to touch him.

questions.question: True or False: According to Luke 7:50, Jesus told the woman that her faith had saved her and sent her away in peace.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 7:50 explicitly states Jesus said to the woman, 'Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace.'

questions.question: True or False: In Luke 7:46, Jesus criticized the woman for not anointing His head with oil.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 7:46 records Jesus saying that Simon did not anoint his head with oil, but the woman anointed his feet with ointment, so the criticism was directed at Simon, not the woman.

theological.title: Luke Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Luke Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 7:9 teach about faith?
options: Faith is the greatest evidence of God's kingdom among all people, including Gentiles
Faith is secondary to works in demonstrating righteousness
Faith must be accompanied by ritual purity to be effective
Faith is limited to the people of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Faith is the greatest evidence of God's kingdom among all people, including Gentiles
questions.explanation: Luke 7:9 shows Jesus marveling at the centurion's faith, saying he has not found so great faith, not even in Israel, indicating faith transcends ethnic boundaries and is a key evidence of God's kingdom.

questions.question: What doctrine about the kingdom of God is taught in Luke 7:28?
options: Those least in the kingdom of God are greater than the greatest prophet born of women
John the Baptist is the least significant figure in the kingdom of God
The kingdom of God is only for prophets and priests
Prophets are greater than any member of the kingdom of God
questions.correctAnswer: Those least in the kingdom of God are greater than the greatest prophet born of women
questions.explanation: Luke 7:28 states that among those born of women there is no greater prophet than John the Baptist, but the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he, teaching the surpassing greatness of the kingdom.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding forgiveness and love does Luke 7:47 teach?
options: The extent of one’s love corresponds to the extent of one’s forgiveness
Forgiveness must be earned by works before love can arise
Only those who sin little can love much
questions.correctAnswer: The extent of one’s love corresponds to the extent of one’s forgiveness
questions.explanation: Luke 7:47 teaches that her many sins are forgiven because she loved much, but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little, directly connecting forgiveness and love.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 7:13 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Compassion
questions.explanation: Luke 7:13 states 'When the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her,' demonstrating God's attribute of compassion toward human suffering.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 7:22 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty over sickness and sin
questions.explanation: Luke 7:22 lists the miracles Jesus performs—healing the blind, lame, lepers, raising the dead, and preaching to the poor—showing his sovereign power over sickness and sin.

questions.question: How does the raising of the widow’s son at Nain in Luke 7:14-15 connect to the broader biblical theme of resurrection?
options: It prefigures Jesus’ own resurrection and the future resurrection of believers
It is an isolated miracle with no theological connection
It demonstrates that resurrection is only for prophets
It shows that resurrection is a reward for perfect obedience
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures Jesus’ own resurrection and the future resurrection of believers
questions.explanation: The raising of the widow’s son in Luke 7:14-15 anticipates the resurrection of Jesus and the general resurrection promised to believers, illustrating God’s power over death.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme is prepared by the questioning of Jesus’ identity by John’s disciples in Luke 7:19-20?
options: The messianic fulfillment and inauguration of the kingdom of God
The rejection of Jesus by Israel
The end of the prophetic office
The establishment of a new political kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: The messianic fulfillment and inauguration of the kingdom of God
questions.explanation: John’s disciples asking if Jesus is 'he that should come' (Luke 7:19-20) points to the fulfillment of messianic prophecy and the inauguration of God’s kingdom through Jesus’ works.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 7:36-38 and Luke 7:47 teach about repentance and forgiveness?
options: True repentance involves heartfelt love and results in forgiveness
Forgiveness is a mere legal declaration without emotional response
Repentance must be public to receive forgiveness
questions.correctAnswer: True repentance involves heartfelt love and results in forgiveness
questions.explanation: Luke 7:36-38 shows the woman’s tears and anointing as a sign of repentance and love, and Luke 7:47 connects her many sins forgiven with her great love, teaching that repentance expresses itself in love and receives forgiveness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 7:9 and Luke 7:23 teach about faith and perseverance in salvation?
options: Great faith is recognized by God, and perseverance in faith leads to blessing
Faith alone is insufficient without works
Faith is only credited to Israelites
Those offended by Jesus will receive blessings
questions.correctAnswer: Great faith is recognized by God, and perseverance in faith leads to blessing
questions.explanation: Luke 7:9 praises the centurion’s great faith, and Luke 7:23 blesses those not offended in Jesus, together affirming that recognized faith and perseverance are key to salvation blessings.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 7:41-43 and Luke 7:50 teach about forgiveness and love in salvation?
options: Forgiveness leads to love, and faith in Christ brings salvation and peace
Debt and forgiveness are purely legal terms without relational impact
Love causes forgiveness rather than results from it
Salvation depends on the amount of debt forgiven
questions.correctAnswer: Forgiveness leads to love, and faith in Christ brings salvation and peace
questions.explanation: Luke 7:41-43 teaches that the one forgiven more loves more, and Luke 7:50 says the woman’s faith saved her and granted peace, connecting forgiveness, love, faith, and salvation.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Jesus was merely a social reformer who tolerated sin. What does Luke 7:36-50 actually teach about Jesus’ attitude toward sin and forgiveness?
options: Jesus forgives sins based on faith and calls for heartfelt repentance
Jesus ignores sin and promotes moral relativism
Jesus condemns sinners without offering forgiveness
Jesus only associates with the righteous and avoids sinners
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus forgives sins based on faith and calls for heartfelt repentance
questions.explanation: Luke 7:36-50 shows Jesus forgiving the woman’s many sins because of her faith and love, not ignoring sin but offering forgiveness through repentance.

questions.question: What doctrine about judgment and rejection is taught in Luke 7:30?
options: Rejecting God’s counsel results in self-condemnation
Rejection of God’s word has no consequences
Pharisees were justified in rejecting baptism
questions.correctAnswer: Rejecting God’s counsel results in self-condemnation
questions.explanation: Luke 7:30 states the Pharisees and lawyers rejected God’s counsel against themselves by not being baptized, teaching that rejection leads to self-condemnation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 7:17 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: Luke 7:17 reports that the rumor of Jesus spread throughout Judea and surrounding regions, indicating God’s providential spreading of Jesus’ fame for redemptive purposes.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection is illustrated by Luke 7:27’s reference to John the Baptist as the messenger preparing the way?
options: John fulfills Malachi’s prophecy, preparing Israel for the Messiah
John is an independent religious leader unrelated to Jesus
John’s role is only symbolic without real fulfillment
John replaces the Old Testament prophets
questions.correctAnswer: John fulfills Malachi’s prophecy, preparing Israel for the Messiah
questions.explanation: Luke 7:27 identifies John as the messenger sent before the Lord to prepare the way, fulfilling Malachi’s prophecy in the redemptive history of Israel.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s sovereign authority is taught in Luke 7:8?
options: God’s authority extends through delegated power and commands are effective immediately
God’s authority is limited to Israel only
God requires physical presence to act
God’s commands depend on human approval
questions.correctAnswer: God’s authority extends through delegated power and commands are effective immediately
questions.explanation: Luke 7:8 illustrates the centurion’s understanding of authority, paralleling divine authority where a word from God effects immediate obedience, showing God’s sovereign power.
